# GLiNER2.5 regression fixtures

This directory contains inputs and expected results consumed by reusable tests,
generators and validation tools. Keep these files reproducible and bounded:

- `reference_manifest.json`, `requests.json`, model metadata and the three
  reference captures pin the upstream source, dependencies and artifact bytes.
- `models/tensor_inventory.json` stores the 334 tensor names and their base
  shapes once, with explicit small/multilingual shape overrides. Expanding it
  reproduces all three independently captured schemas; shapes are never
  inferred from the native loader.
- Tiny encoder/head, task, decoder, training and optimizer fixtures provide
  expected values. Their source generators and contracts define permissible
  updates; numerical tolerances must not be adjusted to fit a new result.
- `training_job_small_v1` supplies the fixed dataset used by job tests.
- `joint_optimizer_source_v1` retains its authoritative source-only capture,
  contract, generator and tests.

The `tasks`, `training_step`, `training_step_dropout`,
`training_inactive_adapters` and `training_inactive_native_epoch` captures omit
duplicated tensor inventories from their JSON metadata. The pinned SafeTensors
headers supply tensor names, shapes and dtypes. The training captures store
each exact dtype, shape and byte payload once; metadata references share an
existing tensor name when those values match. Parameter identities and dropout
mask bindings remain separate, and consumers resolve the immutable values
before constructing their own mutable training state. The training-step captures
retain all tested losses, gradients, optimizer states, dropout masks and resume
results, with unused routing snapshots and intermediate tensors omitted. All
four training captures were replayed against the pinned tiny Fastino source; every
retained tensor and expected value matched exactly. The JSON retains source
identities and input contracts, and tests validate bounded headers and named
tensor references.

Training captures also share identical metadata in local `shared_metadata`
tables. Typed, bounded indices resolve before the numerical checks; inline
values and references are mutually exclusive. Scalar graph fixtures store
common cotangents once, with complete per-case overrides when needed. The
optimizer fixture shares its ordered base parameter names across profiles.

`preprocessing.json` retains the inputs, tensor arrays and query fields checked
by native preprocessing tests. `regex.json` shares its 57 input texts across
390 programs and keeps all three mode results for every text. The optimizer
group fixture retains the four CPU profiles exercised by the native run test.
Primitive pool intermediates, encoder layer snapshots and PEFT norm diagnostics
are omitted; their forward results, gradients and dropout masks remain. Training
job schemas stay inline in each JSONL row, and the tiny tokenizer is kept once
under `training_step` for native dataset preflight.

The base/multilingual and tiny request-level tensor attachments are optional
diagnostics generated by the source oracle. They are not retained here. Keep
their original capture reports and final expected outputs; benchmark token
parity uses the existing pinned `token_evidence.json`. The reference manifest
explicitly lists retained files, whose absence or corruption must still fail.
Small-checkpoint numerical tensors and the tiny boundary weights/tensors remain
required regression inputs. The three small record-mode tensor attachments
were byte-identical to `legacy_structure.safetensors`; their repeated head
invocations are consolidated into that case. All distinct record/schema
pipeline cases and original source outputs remain.

Do not check in campaign directories containing build logs, executables,
object files, copied source trees, temporary environments, model/adapter output
copies, historical result ledgers, PR handoff reports or every intermediate
attempt. Store new runs under the repository's
ignored `.benchmark-results/gliner25/` directory or an external artifact store.
Use a fresh directory for each attempt; preserve failures and exact source,
model, executable and report hashes with the run.

Keep compact input contracts even when their names mention execution. In
particular, `scripts/gliner25/massive11_execution.json` and its preparation
receipt define the reusable runner's admitted schemas, shards and source pins.

Large optional source captures and published model files remain external.
Tests select them explicitly and skip when absent. A skip does not establish
correctness or qualification. The reusable Python scripts live in
[`scripts/gliner25`](../../scripts/gliner25/); the shared process supervisor
lives there rather than inside a historical campaign archive.

See the [GLiNER2.5 work log](../../../../../work-log/completed/gliner2.5.md)
for implementation context, reproduction entry points, and qualification limits.
